newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks drop in thin Ramadan trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks drop in thin Ramadan trade.

text.p: Jordan's stock market on Sunday saw thin pre-holiday trade as most investors shied away from active buying in the last week of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell a marginal 0.03 percent to 153.24 points in low turnover of 444,294 dinars ($627,533).
Livestock and Poultry was the heaviest traded stock with a 0.02 dinars drop to 0.60 dinars in trade worth 85,825 dinars.
Aside from a handful of stocks, hardly any tangible transactions were made on most of 39 shares traded, dealers said.
The market will close next Saturday for a whole week as the country celebrates the Moslem Eid al-Fitr feast, a public holiday.
Limited institututional buying accompanied by some select foreign purchases has kept the bourse afloat in the traditionally quiet Ramadan month.

Sunday's top gainer was Industrial Development Bank which rose 2.16 percent to 2.37 dinars on prospects of healthy 1996 results. Bluechip heavy weight Arab Bank shed 1.00 dinars to 256 dinars in low trade worth only 51,170 dinars.
Overall, losing shares outnumbered gainers by 15 to 12, with shares in another 12 companies traded unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.09 percent to 81.36 points.
